rows.title: Coronavirus And The Labor Market
rows.standfirst: Today's healthy jobs report was uncontaminated by the coronavirus outbreak, but some parts of the labor market may be especially vulnerable in the months ahead.

rows.title: U.S. Added 273,000 Jobs Last Month, But Economists Brace For Coronavirus Impact
rows.standfirst: The increase was about 100,000 more than expected and unemployment dipped to 3.5%. The labor market appears resilient, but fears are growing that the coronavirus will take a toll on the economy.

rows.title: Mortgage Rates Fall To Record Lows. Does It Make Sense To Refinance?
rows.standfirst: Americans are jumping at the chance to save a lot of money by refinancing their home loans — as mortgage rates fall to record lows. Why are rates so low, and when does it pay to refinance?

rows.title: Respirators Key To Coronavirus Battle But They Must Be Worn Correctly
rows.standfirst: A respirator is a central piece of protective gear vital for keeping health care workers healthy — but wearing one incorrectly can put the wearer at risk.

rows.title: Paid Family Leave Bill Faces An Uphill Fight In Colorado
rows.standfirst: Eight states and Washington, D.C., have paid family leave programs funded through payroll taxes. But a similar bill in blue-state Colorado is being watered down.

rows.title: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon Recovering From Heart Surgery
rows.standfirst: Dimon, 63, who is the longest-serving head of a major U.S. bank, experienced "an acute aortic dissection" and underwent surgery to repair it Thursday morning, a JPMorgan memo said.

rows.title: Health Policy Is Economic Policy
rows.standfirst: U.S. policymakers are taking steps to limit the spread and impact of coronavirus. But they're not helped by American health policy, which could use an overhaul if it's to limit the spread of viral outbreaks.

rows.title: Coronavirus Concerns Stymie Live Music Performances And SXSW
rows.standfirst: Organizers, public officials, musicians and other performers are very publicly grappling with competing priorities — and are trying to find innovative ways to deal with canceled events worldwide.

rows.title: Amazon, Facebook, Google, Microsoft Tell Seattle Workers To Stay Home
rows.standfirst: U.S. companies are trying to limit disruption from the coronavirus outbreak by curtailing travel and telling some employees to work from home. Several major tech firms are among the latest to act.

rows.title: Coronavirus Spreads Recession Fears Around The World
rows.standfirst: U.S. businesses are shutting down plants and watching their sales plummet around the world. Many economists now say odds are increasing that the economy will slow, if not contract altogether.

rows.title: A Push To Get More Women On Corporate Boards Gains Momentum
rows.standfirst: At the largest U.S. companies, only about one in five board members are women. In California, more companies are adding them after the state passed a law mandating gender diversity in boardrooms.

rows.title: Not Enough Face Masks Are Made In America To Deal With Coronavirus
rows.standfirst: A global shortage of face masks is prompting concern for the safety of health care workers. Now the U.S. government is trying to bring back an industry that largely left the country years ago.

rows.title: The Corona Bump
rows.standfirst: As coronavirus wreaks havoc on the global economy, some businesses are actually experiencing a boom in demand. Today on the show, what happens when everyone suddenly wants to panic-buy your product.

rows.title: States Take The Wheel Promoting Electric Vehicles
rows.standfirst: There are nearly 1.5 million electric vehicles in the U.S. today. E.V. boosters want more government incentives to increase that. With little federal movement states like New Jersey are taking action.

rows.title: Twitter Vows That As Disinformation Tactics Change, Its Policies Will Keep Pace
rows.standfirst: Twitter's new policy attempts to flag and provide greater context for content that the platform believes to have been "significantly and deceptively altered or fabricated."

rows.title: Grocery Stores Start To Cut Hours As Coronavirus Prompts Surge In Panic-Buying
rows.standfirst: Chains from Walmart and Target to Whole Foods and Publix are cutting back hours to give employees more time to restock shelves and sanitize stores.

rows.title: TSA Screeners' Union Wants More Guidance On Avoiding Coronavirus
rows.standfirst: Three screeners at the San Jose, Calif., airport tested positive, and others may have been exposed. "All we've been told is 'Wash your hands. Don't touch your face,' " a union official said.

rows.title: Trump Steps In To Help Oil Industry Facing Its Own Coronavirus Crisis
rows.standfirst: The oil industry has faced reduced demand from coronavirus, made worse by a global price war. The Trump administration says it will help by buying up cheap oil for the nation's strategic reserve.

rows.title: Medicine For The Economy
rows.standfirst: COVID-19 is hammering our economy. We ask three super smart economists what we should do about it. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: Economic Fear Factor
rows.standfirst: The global economy is being hammered this week - markets have tanked, businesses are closing down. The spreading virus is part of it, but most of the effect is coming from fear.

rows.title: U.S. Coronavirus Testing Gets A Potential Breakthrough
rows.standfirst: U.S. public health experts say they're "flying blind" because they need much more testing to know how widespread the outbreak is. But a just-approved test could be a game-changer.

rows.title: Not Employees: Gig Workers Like Uber Drivers Aren't Eligible For Sick Leave
rows.standfirst: The outbreak is creating uncertainty for Uber drivers and other gig workers, who face difficult choices about whether to work or stay home and lose their livelihoods.

rows.title: Something's Wrong: Stock Sell-Off Exposes Weak Links In Financial System
rows.standfirst: The worry is that bankers, traders and big funds might suddenly find themselves out of cash. Such a scenario could create an ugly spiral throughout the economy.

rows.title: Gas Prices Are Approaching $2
rows.standfirst: Drivers are saving money at the pump, but that's a small silver lining in the big gray cloud of coronavirus-related economic turmoil. AAA says the national average could dive to $2 per gallon soon.

rows.title: Dow Soars Nearly 2,000 Points In Rebound From Biggest Drop Since 1987
rows.standfirst: The Dow Jones Industrial Average and other major stock indexes jumped as President Trump declared a national emergency to deal with the coronavirus pandemic.

rows.title: Nick Hanauer: How Do We Begin To Reinvent Capitalism?
rows.standfirst: Billionaire entrepreneur Nick Hanauer says that today's inequality results from decades of bad economic theory. He argues for a reinvention of our capitalist system and our definition of prosperity.

rows.title: Amid Coronavirus-Related Economic Turmoil, Gas Prices Hit A Low
rows.standfirst: Gas prices have dropped as Saudi Arabia and Russia send the price of crude oil plummeting. That's helping drivers save money but is hurting oil producers around the globe.

rows.title: Are You Affected By Coronavirus-Related Layoffs Or Pay Cuts?
rows.standfirst: Has the coronavirus outbreak affected your employment or income? NPR wants to hear your story.

rows.title: Stocks Enter Bear Market. What Does It Mean?
rows.standfirst: Analysts like to say that the stock market is not the economy. But a bear market reflects concerns and anxieties about the economy, and at times a bear market is accompanied by a recession.

rows.title: Healthcare And Economic Despair
rows.standfirst: The U.S. spends more on healthcare as a share of its economy than any other wealthy country. In addition to making care less affordable, that also causes indirect damage to the rest of the economy.

rows.title: In Ohio And Texas, A Debate Over Whether Abortion Is 'Essential Service'
rows.standfirst: Abortion rights groups say the coronarvirus crisis is being used as a cover to restrict abortion access statewide.

rows.title: Coronavirus Threatens Rural Hospitals Already At The Financial Brink
rows.standfirst: About half of U.S. rural hospitals operate in the red on a good day. Now facing a pandemic, hospital CEOs warn that, without federal help, their doors may close when the community most needs them.

rows.title: United Airlines Threatens To Cut Jobs If Coronavirus Aid Package Isn't Passed
rows.standfirst: Individuals and businesses are slashing air travel. For example, about 624,000 people passed through airport security checkpoints Thursday, compared to 2.4 million people on the same day last year.

rows.title: Make That Quad Long Shot Grande In A Venti Cup To Go; Starbucks Responds To COVID-19
rows.standfirst: Company-operated cafes will close for the next two weeks but coffee drinkers will be able to get a caffeine fix via drive-thru windows or the company's delivery app.

rows.title: Funeral Homes Change Their Practices In Response To Coronavirus
rows.standfirst: In many states, officials have mandated how many people can gather in one space at a time. Some funeral directors ask mourners to stand six feet apart and implore priests and other clergy to be brief.

rows.title: Many Cities Halt Evictions, But Renters Still Need Help
rows.standfirst: In the midst of a pandemic where people are supposed to stay home, many municipalities have halted evictions. But housing advocates want to see more action to help people who can't pay rent.

rows.title: Our COVID-19 Indicators Of The Week
rows.standfirst: Zero and 27 are our indicators of the week. Zero (or nearly zero) is the Fed's new benchmark interest rate. 27 is the number of days that around half of small businesses in the U.S. can go without making money.

rows.title: America's Shopping List: Here's What We're Buying The Most
rows.standfirst: Thermometers and cleaning supplies are seeing spikes in demand, predictably — but now so are snacks and perishable food items. See the latest rundown of what's been selling.

rows.title: U.S. Economic Slowdown In Coming Months Expected To Be Worst On Record
rows.standfirst: Forecasters say the government's aggressive efforts to curtail the spread of the virus will trigger the sharpest slowdown on record. Some see the economy shrinking a staggering 24%.

rows.title: We're Barreling Toward An Epic Glut Of Oil
rows.standfirst: The supply of oil has surged as the coronavirus pandemic has destroyed demand. Prices have plummeted and analysts are starting to ask if the world will have enough space to store all the extra oil.

rows.title: Tax Deadline Extended To July 15 Over Coronavirus Pandemic
rows.standfirst: "All taxpayers and businesses will have this additional time to file and make payments without interest or penalties," Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said Friday.

rows.title: Margrethe Vestager: How Can We Ensure Fair Competition Online?
rows.standfirst: When we shop in a store, we're used to having options. But in a digital economy controlled by tech monopolies, choice isn't built in. Margrethe Vestager is on a mission to change that.

rows.title: Edward Snowden: Why Does Online Privacy Matter?
rows.standfirst: Edward Snowden revealed government programs that collected our private data. Today, he says private corporations have become just as intrusive—but without the restraints placed on government.

rows.title: Dow's Dive Erases All Gains Under Trump
rows.standfirst: The Dow fell more than 900 points, leaving the index 2.8% lower than when President Trump took office. The drop culminated a staggering week of losses as the coronavirus impact took an economic toll.

rows.title: How To Save The Economy Now
rows.standfirst: Neel Kashkari is the President of the Minneapolis Fed. And he's run a bailout of an economy already. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: Feds Warn Merchants Against Coronavirus Treatment Claims
rows.standfirst: The FDA has sent warning letters to seven marketers of products including essential oils, nasal sprays and herbal concoctions. No treatments or vaccines for COVID-19 have been approved.

rows.title: Cruise Ship Struggling With COVID-19 Headed To Florida
rows.standfirst: A cruise ship with four dead and nearly 200 people who have been sick with suspected COVID-19 may dock in Fort Lauderdale if cruise company executives and public officials can agree on a plan.

rows.title: Justice Department Looking Into Senator's Stock Sell-Off
rows.standfirst: Senate Intelligence Committee Chairman Richard Burr sold off a large amount of stocks before the coronavirus market crash. The FBI will assess whether he was motivated by nonpublic information.

rows.title: The Race To Make Ventilators
rows.standfirst: Ventilators are the supply and demand problem of the COVID pandemic. We go inside the scramble to build more, fast. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: Scarcity In The Emergency Room
rows.standfirst: Emergency rooms all over the country are struggling with limited resources: masks, ventilators, hospital beds, doctors. We talk to one ER doctor in New York about how she is managing those resources right now.

rows.title: HHS To Help Companies Develop COVID-19 Vaccines
rows.standfirst: The Department of Health and Human Services outlines support for Moderna and Johnson & Johnson, as the companies work to develop coronavirus vaccines. Beefing up manufacturing capacity is a priority.

rows.title: Economy On Lockdown: Jobless Rate Could Be Highest Since WWII
rows.standfirst: As efforts to slow the coronavirus pandemic temporarily put millions of Americans out of work, forecasters are predicting a record slowdown in the U.S. economy.

rows.title: Walmart To Start Checking Workers' Temperatures
rows.standfirst: The retailer also plans to distribute masks and gloves to workers and add one-way aisles. The company continues to urge shoppers to be "prudent" in stocking up on toilet paper and other supplies.

rows.title: New York Mayor, Attorney General Seek Investigations Over Fired Amazon Worker
rows.standfirst: The warehouse employee helped organize a walkout to demand closure of the facility following several COVID-19 cases. Amazon fired him the same day, saying he violated quarantine and safety measures.

rows.title: Average Gas Prices Are Below $2. A Few Stations Are Even Selling For Under $1
rows.standfirst: AAA says the national average is $1.997 per gallon and it's expected to drop further in the coming weeks. In a few places it's less than half that, but most Americans aren't driving much these days.

rows.title: Builder Of Controversial Keystone XL Pipeline Says It's Moving Forward
rows.standfirst: The final decision to build the project comes after a decade of protests and political reversals in the U.S. Now critics say construction poses a new risk with the coronavirus pandemic.

rows.title: Brooklyn Navy Yard Businesses Mobilize To Help Fight Coronavirus Pandemic
rows.standfirst: During World War II, the Brooklyn Navy Yard repaired warships. Today businesses on the same site are retooling to make medical supplies.

rows.title: Trump Administration Weakens Auto Emissions Standards
rows.standfirst: The Trump administration is replacing Obama-era fuel economy standards with weaker ones that will allow for more air pollution. Groups are already lining up to challenge the new rule.

rows.title: CNN Anchor Chris Cuomo Says He Tested Positive For The Coronavirus
rows.standfirst: The brother of New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo says he has experienced COVID-19 symptoms, including "fever, chills and shortness of breath."

rows.title: The Dow Has Lost Nearly 14% In A Volatile Month
rows.standfirst: The stock market has never seen a month like March, with downs and ups of thousands of points in a day. The Dow has recovered from recent lows, but it has fallen 24% since its record high.
